documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are solid: full VIN that decodes correctly, itemised asking price with a fee-inclusive statement, plus AutoTrader history badges for single owner and no reported accident. The maintenance half is entirely missing — the timing belt, water pump, radiator, CV axles, control-arm bushings and all four brake jobs exist only as dealer advertising copy with no invoice, date, mileage or parts list, and no campaign printout for the dash recall.

condition.rationale: Nothing is stated wrong, and there is partial visible evidence of good condition: the blue car photographs clean and straight, sits level with no rear sag, and wears four fresh matching all-terrain tires on new wheels. Against that, there are no underbody, engine-bay, interior or cluster photos of this VIN, no scan data, and the entire recent-service story is unverified, so the 2UZ's known items (exhaust manifold cracks, radiator, transfer case/diff fluid, steering-rack and timing-cover seepage) remain unexamined.

price_value.rationale: At $25,995 the car sits roughly 48% above the mileage-adjusted fair-value mid of $17,550 and above the top of the $13,015–$18,597 band. Sold comps support this: a 90k-mile Sport Package went $22,800 on BaT and a 129k-mile 2008 went $24,000, both stock-ish. The profile's market note is that heavily modified builds trade at a discount to documented stock examples, yet this one is priced at a dealer-build premium with the service evidence still unproduced.

mission_fit.rationale: Body-on-frame V8, low-range 4WD, roof rack and a deleted-air-ride coil setup genuinely supply capability the RX 350 does not, and the lifted-but-mild 32.7-inch tires suit a sleeping platform or rooftop-tent build without hard off-road hardware. Automatic is fine for this branch. It works against the brief only on money and stock-preference: it is above the $10k–19k ideal band and is a modified build rather than the clean unmodified example the profile favours.

logistics.rationale: San Diego is about 372 miles from Carmel — an easy fly-or-drive and a straightforward drive home. It is an in-state car, so California registration is simple and a licensed dealer must supply a valid smog certificate at retail sale. An established storefront dealer with posted hours makes a nearby independent Toyota/Lexus PPI practical to arrange, though inspection access has not actually been confirmed.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Nautical Blue Mica is one of the more sought-after GX470 colours and the non-navigation spec is what enthusiasts prefer for a modern head unit; the bronze Method MR703 / KO3 combination is tasteful rather than garish. Offsetting that, the buyer prefers stock or mostly stock, and this is a dealer 'build' with a lift and deleted factory air suspension — desirable to the overland crowd, a premium the profile does not want to pay for.

ppi_focus: Verify the timing belt job physically: inspect belt condition and markings, water pump weep hole, and check for fresh gaskets/seals against the dealer's claimed service.
Full underbody inspection on a lift: frame rails, rear crossmember, body mounts, and quality of the rear coil conversion hardware and OME shock/spring fitment.
Cooling system: pressure test, inspect the new radiator's brand and fittings, check coolant condition and heater hoses, and confirm no residual overheating history.
Exhaust manifolds: cold-start listen for the classic 2UZ tick and visually inspect both manifolds and the Y-pipe for cracks.
Drivetrain fluids: pull transfer case and both differential fluid samples and check transmission fluid condition and level at temperature.
Steering rack, front timing cover, valve covers, rear main and front axle seals for leakage, plus CV boot condition on the claimed new axles.
Full scan of engine, ABS, VSC and body modules, including any AVS/height-control faults left behind by the air-ride delete.
Brake test after the claimed front and rear job: pad depth, rotor runout, hardware and brake fluid condition.
Suspension geometry and driveline angles after the 2-inch lift: ball joints (recall history), tie rods, driveshaft vibration at 60-75 mph, and tire rub at full lock.
Confirm odometer against door-jamb/service stickers and check the dash for recall-replacement evidence and cracking.
what_would_change_verdict: Producing dated, mileage-stamped invoices for the timing belt/water pump/radiator and the suspension work would move documentation and condition up materially.
A clean independent Toyota/Lexus PPI with photos of a dry, rust-free underside and a no-codes scan would raise condition substantially.
A negotiated price near the fair-value band top (high teens to low twenties) instead of $25,995 would change price_value from a drag into a neutral or positive.
Discovery of a hidden accident, frame damage, a suppressed AVS/check-engine lamp, or a refusal to allow a PPI would push this sharply down.
Evidence the 'fully serviced' claim is cosmetic only — e.g. an original-date water pump or an unaddressed exhaust manifold crack — would undercut the entire premium.
evidence.mission_note: This fits the utility_capability branch on its merits: body-on-frame V8, low range, roof rack and a coil-converted rear end give real camping and gear capability the RX 350 cannot, and the automatic is acceptable in this branch. The tension is purely money and evidence — it is priced well above the mileage-adjusted fair-value band as a modified dealer build whose entire service story is currently unverified advertising copy.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity cleanly: the VIN decodes to a 2004 GX 470 UZJ120L with the 4.7L V8, matching the advertisement, and AutoTrader's history badges report a single owner with no reported accident. It also establishes the hardware — four new matching BFG KO3 285/70R17 tires on Method MR703 wheels are visible with full tread on a level-sitting dark blue car, and the factory rear air suspension is claimed eliminated in favour of an Old Man Emu coil setup, which is the outcome the profile prefers over aging bags. What it does not establish is the mechanical work: the timing belt, water pump, radiator, CV axles, control-arm bushings and four-corner brake job are listed in all-caps advertising copy with no invoice, no date, no mileage and no parts brands, and the dash-recall completion is likewise unproven. Frame and underbody condition, cluster warning lights, AVS/height-control status after the delete, and transfer case/differential fluid history are all unexamined here; the captured photo set is mostly other GX bodies on the same lot, so only the exterior of this car is visible. On price, $25,995 sits roughly 48% above the mileage-adjusted fair-value mid of $17,550 and above the band top of $18,597, while recent sold comps include a 90k-mile Sport Package at $22,800 and a 129k-mile 2008 at $24,000; the profile's own market note says modified builds trade at a discount to documented stock cars. There is also an unexplained gap between the $25,995 fee-inclusive listing price and the $28,815 cash figure on the page. Nothing is disclosed as broken, so no known repair is established, but nothing beyond the tires is proven good either. San Diego at 372 miles is an easy in-state inspection and drive home, which makes resolving the open items straightforward rather than speculative.
